title: CoMLRL Quick Start
content:
This tutorial demonstrates a simple two-agent training task with a length-ratio reward. Both agents receive the same prompt and generate independently; the second agent does not see the first agent’s response. The reward encourages the second output to contain 2–3× as many characters as the first. It does not evaluate story quality or semantic collaboration.
Users can run the example from an installed source checkout:
python examples/story-len-ratio.pyMemory requirements depend on the model, number of agents, batch size, and response length. W&B logging is disabled by default. The --wandb flag enables it; --wandb-project and --wandb-entity are optional.
Import Libraries# import math from functools import partial from datasets import Dataset from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer from comlrl.utils.reward_processor import RewardProcessors from comlrl.trainers.reinforce import MAGRPOConfig, MAGRPOTrainerDataset Preparation# The dataset contains creative prompts for both agents.
train_data = { "prompt": [ "Describe a city in the clouds:", "Invent a new holiday and explain it:", "Write a bedtime story for a dragon:", "Explain how teleportation might work:", "Tell a joke about dinosaurs:", "Describe a world without electricity:", "Create a superhero with a unique power:", "Write a scene where the moon talks:", "Invent a new type of fruit:", "Design a playground on Mars:", ] } train_dataset = Dataset.from_dict(train_data)Agent Initialization# The tokenizer converts text into model tokens. Each agent uses a separate model instance.
model_name = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name) agents = [AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name) for _ in range(2)]Define the Reward Function# The reward function evaluates the ratio of the agents’ output lengths. It returns the maximum reward (1.0) when the second output contains 2–3× as many characters as the first. Outside this range, the reward decays exponentially with the distance from the nearest boundary.
def proper_length_ratio_reward( completions1, completions2, target_min=2.0, target_max=3.0 ): rewards = [] for c1, c2 in zip(completions1, completions2): len1, len2 = len(c1), len(c2) if len1 == 0: rewards.append(0.0) continue ratio = len2 / len1 if target_min <= ratio <= target_max: reward = 1.0 else: if ratio < target_min: distance = target_min - ratio else: distance = ratio - target_max reward = math.exp(-distance) rewards.append(float(reward)) return rewardsConfigure Training# Users can configure training through MAGRPOConfig, including the learning rate, batch size, and number of generations per agent per prompt.
output_dir = "./magrpo_multi_reward_output" config = MAGRPOConfig( num_train_epochs=3, agent_learning_rate=5e-5, logging_steps=10, num_generations=8, num_turns=1, max_new_tokens=128, )Create the Trainer# The following example initializes MAGRPOTrainer with the agents, reward function, and configuration defined above. RewardProcessors.scale multiplies task rewards by 100. With the default advantage_normalization=True, normalization largely cancels this positive scaling, so it does not imply a 100× stronger policy gradient.
configured_reward_func = partial( proper_length_ratio_reward, target_min=2, target_max=3 ) trainer = MAGRPOTrainer( agents=agents, reward_func=configured_reward_func, reward_processor=RewardProcessors.scale(factor=100.0), args=config, train_dataset=train_dataset, tokenizer=tokenizer, )Run Training# The following code trains both agents to maximize the shared reward and saves the trained models.
trainer.train() trainer.save_model(f"{output_dir}/models")

title: Installation
content:
CoMLRL can be installed from PyPI, conda-forge, or source. Python 3.10 or later is largely recommended. Users can install a PyTorch build compatible with their device.
Installation from PyPI# pip install comlrl # Install PyTorch compatible with your device.Installation from conda-forge# conda install -c conda-forge comlrl # Install PyTorch compatible with your device.Installation from source# Users can clone the repository and install CoMLRL in editable mode to access the latest features or develop it locally:
git clone https://github.com/OpenMLRL/CoMLRL.git cd CoMLRL pip install -e . # Install PyTorch compatible with your device.

title: Multi-Agent REINFORCE
content:
REINFORCE is a class of policy-gradient methods that optimize the policy directly using sampled returns. These methods are widely used for LLM fine-tuning because of their simplicity and efficiency. Examples include GRPO, Dr. GRPO, RLOO, ReMax, TreeRPO, and REINFORCE++. REINFORCE can be extended to multi-agent settings, where multiple LLM agents respond at each turn and their joint responses receive a shared reward.
MAREINFORCE# The policy-gradient surrogate for Multi-Agent REINFORCE (MAREINFORCE), before advantage normalization or reference regularization, can be expressed as:
\[ J(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{o}_0 \sim \mathcal{D}, \mathbf{h}_t \sim \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} \Bigg[\sum_{t=0}^{H-1} R_t \cdot \log \pi_{\theta_i}(a_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})\Bigg], \] where \( R_t \) is the return at turn \( t \) and \( H \) is the horizon (i.e., the number of dialog turns). The expectation is taken over initial observations from the dataset \( \mathcal{D} \) and the joint action history of all episodes following policy \( \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \).
REINFORCE methods do not use a critic model for value estimation. Their policy-gradient estimates can have high variance due to stochastic sampling and long-term credit assignment. Common approaches to reducing this variance include using an action-independent baseline or averaging over more samples, such as \( K \) samples at each joint history \( \mathbf{h}_t \).
\[ J(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{o}_0 \sim \mathcal{D}, \mathbf{h}_t \sim \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} \Bigg[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} \sum_{t=0}^{H-1} \left(R^{k}_t - b(\mathbf{h}_t)\right) \cdot \log \pi_{\theta_i}(a^{k}_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})\Bigg], \] where the baseline \( b(\mathbf{h}_t) \) is action-independent.
MAGRPO# Multi-Agent Group-Relative Policy Optimization (MAGRPO) is an instantiation of MAREINFORCE inspired by GRPO, where the group-average baseline is the mean return of \( K \) samples. In the default aligned joint mode, its surrogate before advantage normalization is:
\[ J(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{o}_0 \sim \mathcal{D}, \mathbf{h}_t \sim \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} \Bigg[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{t=0}^{H-1} \left(R^{k}_t - \frac{1}{K}\sum_{l=1}^{K}R^{l}_t\right) \cdot \log \pi_{\theta_i}(a^{k}_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})\Bigg]. \] The sampled group mean includes the sample being updated, so it is not the action-independent baseline assumed in the general expression above. In multi-turn training, each branch’s return is its immediate reward plus the mean return of its child node, with no discount applied. In cross mode, each agent’s completion instead receives the sum of returns over all joint combinations containing that completion.
By default, advantage_normalization=True then centers and scales the advantages within each node’s generation group using the population standard deviation, with a minimum denominator of 1e-6. If reference KL regularization is enabled, the sampled reference penalty is subtracted from returns before the baseline and normalization are applied.
MAGRPO and the variants below share one trainer loop. At each rollout node, every agent samples \( K \) responses, the trainer scores the index-aligned joint responses with one shared reward, and each agent weights its own log-probabilities by the resulting shared advantages before a buffered optimizer step.
MAREINFORCE training step Each agent samples K responses; index-aligned joint responses share one reward and return, a group baseline gives shared advantages, and each agent updates on its own log-probabilities. Complete diagram Play Replay The current MAGRPOTrainer loss slice omits the final completion token, so its implemented sequence score differs from the full sequence log-probability in the surrogate above. The canonical setting is joint_mode="cross"; the accepted "crossed" alias generates Cartesian combinations but does not apply the same per-completion return aggregation.
MAGRPOConfig Parameters num_agents: Configured number of agents, which should match the trainer setup num_turns: Number of turns per episode num_train_epochs: Number of training epochs agent_learning_rate: Learning rate logging_steps: Logging interval in steps num_generations: Number of generations to sample per prompt for each agent max_new_tokens: Maximum number of new tokens to generate temperature: Temperature for sampling top_p: Top-p for sampling top_k: Top-k for sampling discount: Retained configuration field; the current MAGRPO implementation computes undiscounted returns and does not use this value joint_mode: Joint action composition (aligned for index-aligned, cross for Cartesian product) early_termination_threshold: A training branch stops expanding when its node’s mean immediate reward exceeds this threshold (default -0.2; None disables early termination) rollout_buffer_size: Number of node samples to buffer per agent before an update train_batch_size: Number of node samples per optimizer step; defaults to rollout_buffer_size advantage_normalization: Whether to center and scale advantages within each node’s generation group (default True) eval_interval: Evaluation runs at batch indices divisible by N, including the first batch of each epoch; 0 disables periodic evaluation eval_num_samples: Number of samples to evaluate per evaluation run eval_batch_size: Evaluation DataLoader batch size external_prompt_passthrough: Whether to use external prompts directly in multi-turn training advantage_mode: Baseline mode (mean, max, rloo, raw) parallel_training: Agent execution mode (none or mp) agent_devices: Agent device placement; required explicitly for parallel_training="mp" reference_kl_enabled: Whether to enable a frozen-reference KL penalty (default False) reference_kl_coef: Weight of the reference penalty (default 0.1) reference_devices: Optional device placement for the reference models MAGRPOTrainer Parameters agent_model or agents: Model identifier string for homogeneous agents, or a list of model identifiers or preloaded models; preloaded models are supplied through agents num_agents: Number of agents created from agent_model (default 2), configured independently of args. When only agents is supplied, its length determines the agent count tokenizer: Shared tokenizer or one per agent; optional for model identifiers, required for preloaded models reward_func: Callable that returns a list of floats (required) reward_processor: Optional processor to apply to rewards (e.g., scaling) formatters: Single callable or list of per-agent callables for prompt formatting args: Instance of MAGRPOConfig (optional) train_dataset: Dataset required when calling train() eval_dataset: Evaluation dataset (optional) model_config: Model configuration dictionary (optional) wandb_config: Configuration for Weights & Biases logging (optional) external_transition: Function providing transitions between turns; required when num_turns > 1 (the default is 2) eval_logger: Optional task-metrics callback, called as eval_logger(agent_completions_turns=..., batch_items=..., prompts=...); returns one metrics dictionary per evaluated item and is used with eval_aggregator eval_aggregator: Optional callback, called as eval_aggregator(metrics, num_turns=...); the returned turn_k/... metrics are logged under eval/. Both evaluation callbacks must be supplied for custom metrics MAGRPO collects samples into a rollout buffer and recomputes their log-probabilities during updates, without importance sampling or ratio clipping. Samples may therefore predate earlier updates from the same buffer or rollout tree. Since the trainer has no critic model, value_clip_range does not apply.
The trainer uses a fixed training DataLoader batch size of 1 and requires at least num_generations=2, including for the raw-return variant. By default, train_batch_size=rollout_buffer_size: each agent averages the losses of its buffered node samples for one optimizer step. Smaller mini-batches produce multiple optimizer steps; a partial buffer is flushed at the end of each epoch.
Other Variants# CoMLRL also provides other MAREINFORCE variants with different baselines:
MARLOO: Multi-Agent REINFORCE Leave-One-Out. The baseline is the mean return of the other generations in the same node’s sample group, not the other agents. \[ J(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{o}_0 \sim \mathcal{D}, \mathbf{h}_t \sim \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} \Bigg[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{t=0}^{H-1} \left(R^{k}_t - \frac{1}{K-1}\sum_{l=1, l\neq k}^{K}R^{l}_t\right) \cdot \log \pi_{\theta_i}(a^{k}_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})\Bigg]. \] MAReMax: Multi-Agent REINFORCE with Group Max (MAReMaxConfig and MAReMaxTrainer). The baseline is the maximum sampled group return at the node; this implementation does not generate a separate greedy baseline response. \[ J(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{o}_0 \sim \mathcal{D}, \mathbf{h}_t \sim \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} \Bigg[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{t=0}^{H-1} \left(R^{k}_t - \mathrm{max}_l\, R^l_t \right) \cdot \log \pi_{\theta_i}(a^{k}_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})\Bigg]. \] MAREINFORCETrainer, MARLOOTrainer, and MAReMaxTrainer derive from comlrl.trainers.reinforce.MAGRPOTrainer. Their corresponding configuration classes inherit MAGRPOConfig, with default advantage_mode values of raw, rloo, and max, respectively. They share the same trainer interface and configuration fields.
The four trainers differ only in the baseline subtracted from the shared return. For one node with \( K=4 \) joint responses, the animation below compares their advantages before normalization: MAREINFORCE keeps the raw return, as in REINFORCE; MAGRPO subtracts the group mean, as in GRPO; MARLOO subtracts the mean of the other \( K-1 \) returns, as in RLOO, which scales the MAGRPO advantages by \( K/(K-1) \); and MAReMax subtracts the group maximum, so no response receives a positive advantage.
Baselines across MAREINFORCE variants Each row subtracts a different baseline from the same shared returns; shaded bars mark the advantages before normalization. Complete diagram Play Replay The variant formulas describe advantages before normalization. All variants inherit advantage_normalization=True, which re-centers even raw returns and max-baseline advantages. Except for the standard-deviation floor and numerical precision, the four modes then yield the same normalized advantages. Users can retain the baseline differences shown above, including the raw-return MAREINFORCE estimator, by setting advantage_normalization=False.

title: Multi-Turn Algorithm
content:
Many complex problems require more than one turn to solve. LLM agents interact with the environment to obtain useful feedback from other models or tools in the system.
Multi-Turn MAGRPO# Multi-turn MAGRPO builds a rollout tree whose branches represent different joint responses (TreeRPO).
Joint rollout tree Joint observations and actions branch into independent rollouts. Joint responses branch into independent rollouts Turn 1 Next turn Task Response A Response B Rollout 1 Rollout 2 Rollout 3 Rollout 4 Each branch has its own history Complete diagram Play Replay Each episode begins with a task sampled from the dataset, which provides the initial observations \( \mathbf{o}_0=\{o_{1, 0}, \cdots, o_{n, 0}\} \) and histories \( \mathbf{h}_0=\{h_{1, 0}, \cdots, h_{n, 0}\} \) for all agents. At each turn, agents generate a group of joint responses \( \mathbf{a}^{\mathcal{G}}_t\gets\boldsymbol{\pi}^{\mathcal{G}}(\cdot|\mathbf{h}_t) \) from their current observation-action history \( \mathbf{h}_t \). Each response starts a distinct rollout. Agents receive joint rewards \( r^{(g)}_{t} \) for each response, based on the accumulated history and current joint action \( \mathbf{a}^{(g)}_{t} \in \mathbf{a}^{\mathcal{G}}_{t} \). Each rollout then evolves independently, producing new joint observations \( \mathbf{o}^{\mathcal{G}}_{t+1} \) as the environment evolves and branching into further rollouts at the next turn \( t+1 \). This process continues until the terminal turn \( H \).
Joint Mode# MAGRPO supports two modes for forming joint responses at each turn:
Aligned (joint_mode="aligned"): Responses with the same generation index are combined across agents. Each agent samples \( G \) responses (the fixed num_generations value) at every node. With \( T \) turns and no early termination, the tree has \( G^T \) leaves. Aligned joint responses Responses with matching generation indices are combined across agents. Aligned mode pairs samples with the same generation index Within one rollout 2 joint responses Agent A A1 A2 Agent B B1 B2 Same index A1 B1 A2 B2 Match generation indices Complete diagram Play Replay Cross (joint_mode="cross"): The Cartesian product of the agents’ sampled responses yields \( G^N \) joint actions per node. With no early termination, the tree has \( G^{N \cdot T} \) leaves. Responses are reused across combinations, so the joint samples are not independent. This increases the number of reward evaluations and the rollout size without guaranteeing more accurate value estimates. Cross joint responses The Cartesian product forms joint responses within each rollout. Cross mode forms all pairs within one rollout Within one rollout 4 joint responses Agent A A1 A2 Agent B B1 B2 All pairs A1 B1 A1 B2 A2 B1 A2 B2 Samples are reused across pairs Complete diagram Play Replay Only responses from the same rollout can be combined because rollouts evolve independently. The current MAGRPO implementation accumulates undiscounted returns: discount does not change its tree recursion. MAREINFORCE describes return aggregation and advantage normalization.
Multi-Turn MAAC/IAC# The MAGRPO rollout tree generates numerous samples per episode. In the multi-turn setting, MAAC/IAC generate only one sample per agent per turn, and the episode continues across turns until termination. MAAC/IAC use one-step temporal-difference targets, with discount applied to the next rollout value and no bootstrapping after the final or early-terminated turn. The current implementation collects the full episode before buffering its samples. Policy updates occur when rollout_buffer_size is reached, and any remaining buffer is flushed at the end of the epoch. Policies are not updated between turns of the same episode. External feedback controls how environment observations are incorporated into prompts for subsequent turns. This mechanism is usually implemented in CoMLRL’s downstream environments.
Actor-critic trajectory One joint response per turn advances the episode from left to right. Actor-critic episodes advance one joint response per turn before buffering and updates Turn 1 1 response Turn 2 1 response Final turn 1 response Buffer Full episode Update Policy One joint response per turn At buffer limit or epoch end Complete diagram Play Replay

title: Training Framework
content:
MARLHF and MADPO share a training framework. Actors generate joint responses, and the task reward ranks them to form preference pairs. The iterative trainers repeat this process against a comparator, while a replay buffer selects the pairs for each update. MARLHF and MADPO describe the two learning objectives.
Collaboration Modes# collaboration_mode sets the trainable actor layout, and comparator_generation_mode sets the comparator layout in iterative training.
Actor layout Comparator layout Joint responses Decentralized Decentralized Each role generates its own response on both sides of the comparison. Decentralized Centralized Separate actors are compared with one comparator that generates all roles’ responses. Centralized Centralized One actor and one comparator each generate a complete joint response. The diagram compares the three supported layouts, with the actor on the left and the comparator \( \varpi \) on the right.
Actor and comparator layouts One policy per role on both sides; one policy per role against a comparator whose joint response is split into roles; or one policy on each side writing the whole joint response. Actor and comparator layouts Three supported layouts: per-role actors and per-role comparators; per-role actors with a joint comparator response split into roles; or one actor and one comparator retaining joint text. ActorsComparisonComparator Per-role actors Per-role policies Role responses Per-role actors One joint policy Split into roles One joint actor One joint policy Joint text Complete diagram Play Replay In decentralized mode, each agent has its own policy and response; MADPO combines their preference margins, and MARLHF learns one reward from the joint responses. In centralized mode, one actor receives every role’s prompt and generates the complete joint response.
All four preference trainers currently require num_turns=1 and joint_mode="aligned". Centralized actor training automatically uses a centralized comparator in the iterative trainers; a centralized actor with a decentralized comparator is not supported.
Centralized Preference Collaboration# MADPOConfig, MARLHFConfig, and their iterative variants accept collaboration_mode="centralized" (default "decentralized"). One actor and one optimizer then train on the complete joint response, including the role delimiters, so later roles are conditioned on earlier ones.
The default TaggedCentralizedComparatorAdapter writes indexed <agent_0>...</agent_0> sections. A custom centralized_comparator_adapter can redefine the joint prompt (build_prompt) and the role parser (parse_completion); the same adapter serves the actor and the comparator. Parsing happens only for the task reward and evaluation; replay, learned-reward scoring, and training retain the joint text.
num_agents must equal the number of task roles. Centralized training requires one actor, specified through agent_model once or one entry in agents with its tokenizer. agent_devices and, with reference KL, reference_devices describe one actor; the reward model and an external comparator retain their own device settings. max_new_tokens is the total joint-response budget. For two roles, this is roughly twice a per-role limit. For MARLHF, reward_max_length must also cover the joint prompt and every role’s output. MADPO remains reference-free; MARLHF’s online RL stage applies the configured KL penalty. The iterative trainers require comparator_centralized_agent_index=0; all comparator sources retain their defined behavior. One joint completion counts as one environment step, and a preference pair uses environment_steps_per_pair (default 2). Actor checkpoints contain one actor (agent_0). W&B records collaboration_mode, num_roles, num_actor_models, and the effective comparator generation mode.
Iterative Training# MADPOIterTrainer and MARLHFIterTrainer alternate preference collection with training. Each round compares new samples from the current policy with comparator samples at the same candidate index; either side can win, and ties are skipped. The round’s pairs are stored as \( \mathcal{D}^{(\nu)} \), and the replay buffer selects the training pairs \( \mathcal{B}^{(\nu)} \).
The diagram unrolls one iteration \( \nu \), from sampling against the comparator to the updated policies.
One iterative training round The task reward turns each comparison with the comparator into a preference pair, replay picks training pairs from this and earlier rounds, and MADPO, or a reward model followed by RL, produces the next policies. One iterative training round Current actors and a comparator produce responses. Reward ranking creates preference pairs, replay selects training pairs, and either MADPO or reward-model training followed by RL updates the actors for the next round. Current actors Comparator Rank pairs Replay MADPODirect update MARLHFReward model → RL Updated actors · next round Complete diagram Play Replay MADPOIter runs MADPO updates on the selected pairs for num_train_epochs per iteration. MARLHFIter fits a newly initialized reward model on the selected pairs, then runs the selected online RL algorithm. An iteration is a refresh-and-training round, not a dialog turn. Users can import the iterative configurations and trainers from comlrl.trainers.preference.
MADPOIterConfig Parameters Inherits MADPOConfig; num_train_epochs applies to each iteration num_iterations: Number of refresh-and-training rounds pair_selection: Adds "comparator_reward" (the iterative default), which prefers higher comparator rewards, then larger reward gaps; "all" retains every non-tied comparison and requires preference_pairs_per_sample=None Comparator and replay settings: described in Comparator and Replay Buffer MARLHFIterConfig Parameters Combines the MARLHF settings with the iterative comparator and replay settings preference_scoring_reward: "task" (default) labels new comparisons with the task reward; "reward_model" uses the previous iteration’s reward model once one exists reward_num_train_epochs: Reward-model training epochs per iteration Comparator# The comparator supplies the alternative responses for each comparison. comparator_policy chooses its source, and comparator_generation_mode chooses whether it generates separate role responses or one joint response.
In each iteration, the current actors and the comparator respond to the same task, and every same-index comparison with a clear task-reward winner becomes a preference pair.
Comparator pairs The current actors and the comparator sample for the same task; the task reward decides each same-index comparison in either direction, and the decided comparisons form the iteration's preference pairs. Comparator preference pairs Current actors and a comparator respond to the same task. Same-index candidates are ranked by the task reward. Either side can become the winner; ties are skipped. Task Current actors Comparator Task reward Winner · loserEither side can win Ties skipped Complete diagram Play Replay Policy Response source current (default) Active actor weights, sampled with a separate random-number stream. current_copy Current actor weights, copied to comparator_devices for each collection phase when those differ from the actor devices. model Explicit models from comparator_model_name or comparator_agents. history A saved actor checkpoint from comparator_history_k iterations back; the initial policy until one exists. api A remote model endpoint. The history source saves policy checkpoints automatically. The two sides may sample different numbers of candidates, but only indices present on both sides are compared. pair_selection="comparator_reward" ranks comparisons by comparator reward and then reward gap; it does not assume the comparator wins.
Comparator parameters:
comparator_policy: "current", "current_copy", "model", "history", or "api" comparator_num_candidates: Comparator sample count; defaults to preference_num_candidates comparator_model_name or comparator_agents: Model sources for "model" comparator_history_k: Iterations back for "history"; defaults to 1 comparator_devices: Device placement for local comparator models policy_checkpoint_dir: Optional actor-checkpoint location; setting it also saves checkpoints for the other sources Comparator Generation# With decentralized actors, a decentralized comparator (the default) generates one response per role, while a centralized comparator receives the adapter’s joint prompt and generates all roles’ responses together. Its joint text is then parsed into role responses before pairs are built. With a centralized actor, the comparator’s joint text is retained throughout preference learning.
Comparator generation parameters:
comparator_generation_mode: "decentralized" or "centralized" comparator_centralized_agent_index: Role whose actor or checkpoint generates a centralized comparator’s joint response (current, current-copy, or history sources); defaults to 0, and centralized actor training requires 0 centralized_comparator_adapter: Trainer argument with the shared joint prompt builder and role parser Local Models# Users can specify a shared model source through comparator_model_name, or a list of sources through comparator_agents. A decentralized comparator uses one model per role; a centralized comparator uses one model, chosen by comparator_centralized_agent_index when comparator_agents lists one source per role. Sources can be model repositories or local checkpoints, as described in Model Loading.
comparator_policy=model comparator_model_name=/path/to/comparator-checkpoint comparator_generation_mode=centralized comparator_centralized_agent_index=0 comparator_devices=cuda:1API Comparators# With comparator_policy=api, the comparator queries a remote model. comparator_api_format selects the request format:
generic (default): The request includes the prompt, actor index, task item, candidate count, and generation settings; completions are read from comparator_api_response_field. openai: Chat Completions, also used by compatible endpoints such as DeepSeek’s. anthropic: Anthropic Messages API (https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). openai_responses (alias responses or codex): OpenAI Responses API (https://api.openai.com/v1/responses, OPENAI_API_KEY). The Anthropic and Responses formats have no n parameter, so they send one request per candidate. Requests use the standard centralized or decentralized comparator prompts.
comparator_policy=api comparator_api_format=anthropic comparator_api_url=https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages comparator_api_model=claude-sonnet-4-20250514 comparator_api_key_env=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Comparator API parameters:
comparator_api_url: Endpoint URL; required for "api" comparator_api_format: "generic" (default), "openai", "anthropic", or "openai_responses" comparator_api_model: Model name passed to the endpoint comparator_api_key_env or comparator_api_key: Environment variable holding the key, or the key itself comparator_api_headers: Additional request headers comparator_api_key_header, comparator_api_key_prefix: Authentication header and prefix; default "Authorization" and "Bearer", with native Anthropic header handling comparator_api_timeout: Request timeout in seconds; default 120 comparator_api_max_n_per_request: Maximum candidates per Chat Completions call, for endpoints that limit n comparator_api_response_field: Completions field in a generic response; default "completions" comparator_api_extra_body: Additional request-body fields Replay Buffer# The replay buffer selects which stored pairs are used for training in each round. The current round’s dataset is saved first, so it is eligible alongside earlier rounds.
Mode Eligible preference data current (default) All pairs from the current round, without historical sampling. nearest_k The latest preference_replay_k non-empty round datasets, including the current one. all_history Every non-empty round dataset of the current trainer run. lambda_decay The same history, weighted toward recent rounds. Each row of the diagram shows which round datasets a mode can draw from and how strongly each is weighted, with the newest round on the right.
Replay modes Which of five round datasets each replay mode draws from, and with what weight, before the training pairs are sampled by those weights. Replay selection modes Five round datasets run from oldest to newest. Current uses every current-round pair. Nearest-k samples the latest two non-empty rounds here; all-history samples all stored non-empty rounds equally; lambda-decay favors more recent rounds. OldestNewest current All pairs nearest_kLatest 2 rounds Sample all_history Sample lambda_decay Sample Eligible rounds · selection weight Complete diagram Play Replay nearest_k means the most recent rounds, not nearest-neighbor retrieval. In nearest_k and all_history, eligible datasets have equal weight regardless of size, and historical modes sample from them rather than training on every stored pair.
Lambda Decay# With age \( a=0 \) for the newest of \( K \) eligible datasets, preference_replay_lambda (\( \lambda \)) sets the selection weights:
\[ w_a = \frac{\lambda^a}{\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}\lambda^j}, \qquad 0 \leq \lambda \leq 1. \] \( \lambda=0 \) keeps only the newest dataset, smaller values favor recent rounds, and \( \lambda=1 \) weights every dataset equally.
Sampling# Historical modes assign each of the preference_replay_sample_size draws to a dataset by weight, then sample pairs within each dataset. Sampling proceeds without repetition when the assigned count does not exceed the dataset size; larger counts cycle through shuffled copies. The combined sample is shuffled. The default sample size is the current round’s pair count, or the latest non-empty dataset’s size if the current round is empty.
Replay Buffer parameters:
preference_replay_mode: "current" (default), "nearest_k", "all_history", or "lambda_decay" preference_replay_k: Number of recent non-empty datasets for "nearest_k"; required in that mode preference_replay_lambda: Decay parameter in [0, 1]; required for "lambda_decay" preference_replay_sample_size: Pairs sampled by the historical modes, or None for the default above preference_replay_dir: Optional location of the saved round datasets current rejects preference_replay_sample_size and preference_replay_lambda, and accepts preference_replay_k only as None or 1. The mode-specific options are preference_replay_k for nearest_k and preference_replay_lambda for lambda_decay.
from comlrl.trainers.preference import MADPOIterConfig args = MADPOIterConfig( num_agents=2, preference_replay_mode="lambda_decay", preference_replay_lambda=0.8, preference_replay_sample_size=256, )MARLHFIterConfig accepts the same options. To replay only the latest rounds, users can set preference_replay_mode="nearest_k" and specify the number of rounds through preference_replay_k.
Saved Preference Data# Each round is written to iteration_0001.json, iteration_0002.json, and so on under preference_replay_dir, with the prompts, preferred and rejected completions, rewards, and metadata. Historical samples are re-tokenized from this text. Setting preference_replay_dir to an earlier run alone does not import its files. Training checkpoints restore the replay index and its data. Actor checkpoints for the history comparator are stored separately under policy_checkpoint_dir.

Contributing# Contributions to CoMLRL are welcome. This guide covers issue reporting, code changes, and codebase maintenance.
Development Guidelines# Contributors can fork the upstream repository. The following commands clone the fork and synchronize it with upstream: git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/CoMLRL.git cd CoMLRL git remote add upstream https://github.com/OpenMLRL/CoMLRL.git git fetch upstream git checkout -b feature/<short-description> upstream/main git fetch upstream && git rebase upstream/main Contributors can implement new features or fix bugs and update the documentation as needed. title: Environment Transition
content:
External feedback mechanisms control how environment observations are incorporated into prompts for subsequent turns. These mechanisms are usually implemented in CoMLRL’s downstream environments.
Feedback Loop Agents combine their contributions into a response. Tool errors and user hints or new information are routed back to the corresponding agent for the next turn. Agent 1 Agent 2 Agent 3 Response Toolkit Error User Hint · Info Feedback 1 2 3 Complete diagram Play Replay Custom External Feedback# Users can implement custom external feedback by defining a function with the following interface:
External Feedback Parameters prompt: Original task prompt or problem description (required) agent_completions: List or tuple of completions from the previous turn, one per agent (required) num_agents: Number of agents in the system (required) prompt_history_per_agent: List containing one list of previous prompts per agent (optional) response_history_per_agent: List containing one list of previous responses per agent (optional) The function must return a list or tuple of prompts for the next turn, one for each agent. The trainer passes only the arguments above, with no additional keyword arguments. Users can configure mode-specific parameters through a closure or functools.partial.
By default, each returned prompt becomes the new prompt field and is passed through the corresponding agent’s formatter. If external_prompt_passthrough=true, the returned prompts are used directly without reformatting. In MAGRPO, the external transition is called for each rollout branch with that branch’s histories.
The following example constructs prompts for the next turn:
from typing import List, Optional def custom_external( prompt: str, agent_completions: List[str], num_agents: int, prompt_history_per_agent: Optional[List[List[str]]] = None, response_history_per_agent: Optional[List[List[str]]] = None, ) -> List[str]: # Custom logic to format next-turn prompts # Access environment feedback, tool outputs, etc. next_turn_prompts = [] for i in range(num_agents): # Format prompt for agent i based on history and feedback next_prompt = f"{prompt}\nPrevious attempt: {agent_completions[i]}\nPlease revise." next_turn_prompts.append(next_prompt) return next_turn_prompts IAC/MAAC multi-turn training requires num_generations to be set to 1.
Example Modes# An environment for code generation includes three example external transition modes:
external.mode=expert_edits: An external LLM (default: DeepSeek-Coder) proposes code edits. Follow-up prompts include edit suggestions and context from previous turns. With the required API keys, users can select a different expert (e.g., Claude, GPT) through expert_model.
external.mode=level_feedback: Static AST checks and dynamic code execution provide a diagnosis. By default, the sandbox includes only the first test. The sandbox_slice parameter selects all tests (0, None, or ‘all’) or a specific number of tests (negative values are supported).
external.mode=plain: This self-improvement mode includes only the prompts and responses from previous turns and a revision instruction.

title: Model Loading & Saving
content:
CoMLRL supports both homogeneous and heterogeneous models from Hugging Face or local directories. Users can specify Hugging Face model identifiers through agent_model/critic_model for homogeneous setups, or provide agents/critics lists for heterogeneous setups. Trained agents can be saved and loaded into a new trainer for further training.
Loading LLM Agents# Homogeneous Agents# Users can initialize homogeneous agents by setting agent_model to a single model identifier and leaving agents=None. For trainers with a separate num_agents constructor argument, users can set it alongside the matching configuration value; the configuration alone does not override it.
The following example loads 3x Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B agents:
trainer = MAGRPOTrainer( agent_model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B", agents=None, num_agents=3, reward_func=reward_func, train_dataset=train_dataset, args=MAGRPOConfig(num_agents=3, num_turns=1, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=None), )Heterogeneous Agents# Although homogeneous agents can be prompted to take on different roles and work on separate parts of a task in parallel, heterogeneous agents can also contribute the specialized capabilities of different models.
Users can initialize heterogeneous agents by supplying model identifiers or loaded model objects in agents, with compatible tokenizers supplied through tokenizer. With agents supplied, agent_model can remain None. If both are provided, their model names must match, and their list lengths must match the number of agents; otherwise, training raises an error.
The following example loads Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B + Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B agents:
trainer = MAGRPOTrainer( agent_model=None, agents=["Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B"], reward_func=reward_func, train_dataset=train_dataset, args=MAGRPOConfig(num_agents=2, num_turns=1, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=None), )Loading LLM Critics# Algorithms such as Independent Actor-Critic (IAC) and Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (MAAC) use LLM critics. How these critics are loaded depends on the algorithm and the use_separate_critic setting.
Centralized Critic# Users can load a separate centralized critic through critic_model or a one-element critics list. It must be a supported causal language model: the trainer adds a value head and encodes the joint input with the first actor’s tokenizer, so that tokenizer must also be compatible with the critic.
The following example pairs Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B + Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B actors with a centralized Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B critic:
trainer = MAACTrainer( agent_model=None, agents=["Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B"], tokenizer=[ AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B"), AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B"), ], critic_model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B", critics=None, reward_func=reward_func, train_dataset=train_dataset, args=MAACConfig(num_agents=2, num_turns=1, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=None), )Independent Critics# With independent critics, each agent can have its own critic. With use_separate_critic=True, users can supply one critic_model identifier to load a separate copy per agent, or a critics list of length num_agents. Each separate critic receives token IDs from its actor’s tokenizer and must be compatible with it. With use_separate_critic=false, each actor and critic share an LLM backbone and load together. In this case, critic_model and critics remain unset (null or None). As with agents, supplying both critic_model and critics requires matching model names and lengths; otherwise, training raises an error.
The following example loads Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B + Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B actors with separate critics based on the same models:
trainer = IACTrainer( agent_model=None, agents=["Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B"], tokenizer=[ AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B"), AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B"), ], critic_model=None, critics=["Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B"], reward_func=reward_func, train_dataset=train_dataset, args=IACConfig( num_agents=2, num_turns=1, use_separate_critic=True, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=None, ), )Alternatively, each actor can share the same model with its critic:
trainer = IACTrainer( agent_model=None, agents=["Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B"], tokenizer=[ AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B"), AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B"), ], critic_model=None, critics=None, reward_func=reward_func, train_dataset=train_dataset, args=IACConfig( num_agents=2, num_turns=1, use_separate_critic=False, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=None, ), ) Trainers use agents/critics lists internally. The agent_model and critic_model parameters are shortcuts for homogeneous setups and must be consistent with any corresponding lists supplied.
MAGRPO loads tokenizers automatically for model identifier strings. MAAC/IAC load a tokenizer automatically for agent_model, but require an explicit tokenizer when agents is supplied, even if it contains strings. Loaded model objects require one compatible shared tokenizer or a tokenizer list matching the actors. Heterogeneous actors may have different vocabularies when each uses its own compatible tokenizer; separate critics must also accept their actor’s token IDs (the first actor’s IDs for MAAC).
Saving & Resuming Training# Saving Models# Users can call save_model(output_dir) after training to explicitly save the actors’ Hugging Face model configurations, weights, and tokenizers to local directories:
trainer.train() trainer.save_model("./saved-models/run-1")Training from Saved Models# Users can continue training a saved two-actor MAGRPO setup by supplying the actors’ directories in the original role order. The parent run-1 directory contains the actors; each agent_i directory is a loadable model.
from comlrl.trainers.reinforce import MAGRPOConfig, MAGRPOTrainer continued_trainer = MAGRPOTrainer( agents=[ "./saved-models/run-1/agent_0", "./saved-models/run-1/agent_1", ], num_agents=2, reward_func=reward_func, train_dataset=train_dataset, args=MAGRPOConfig( num_agents=2, num_turns=1, num_train_epochs=3, agent_learning_rate=5e-6, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=None, ), ) continued_trainer.train() continued_trainer.save_model("./saved-models/run-2")MAGRPO loads tokenizers from the actor directories automatically. Here, num_train_epochs=3 means three epochs in the new training run. The dataset, reward function, training configuration, and any custom formatters, reward processor, or external transition must be supplied again; save_model does not store them.
Other trainers support the same local-directory approach, subject to the tokenizer and actor-count requirements above. Preference trainers start preference collection and reward learning according to the new run’s configuration.
Restoring Value Heads# This section applies to save_model exports. Training checkpoints restore value heads automatically.
IAC and MAAC save value heads separately as value_head.pt. Loading a critic or shared actor directory through the constructor restores the language-model backbone and creates a new value head. Users can retain the learned values by explicitly restoring the saved head before calling train().
For a saved two-actor MAAC setup using the default linear value head:
from pathlib import Path import torch from transformers import AutoTokenizer from comlrl.trainers.actor_critic import MAACConfig, MAACTrainer saved_dir = Path("./saved-models/maac-run-1") actor_dirs = [str(saved_dir / f"agent_{i}") for i in range(2)] continued_maac = MAACTrainer( agents=actor_dirs, tokenizer=[AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path) for path in actor_dirs], critic_model=str(saved_dir / "critic"), reward_func=reward_func, train_dataset=train_dataset, args=MAACConfig(num_agents=2, num_turns=1, num_train_epochs=3), ) continued_maac.critics[0].value_head.load_state_dict( torch.load( saved_dir / "critic" / "value_head.pt", map_location="cpu", weights_only=True, ) ) continued_maac.train() continued_maac.save_model("./saved-models/maac-run-2")For IAC, the same load_state_dict step applies to continued_iac.agents[i].value_head when use_separate_critic=False, or to continued_iac.critics[i].value_head when it is True. Separate critic backbones also require loading through critic_model or critics.
The value-head architecture must match the saved run. IAC requires the original IACConfig.value_head_hidden_dim for shared heads and IACConfig.critic_value_head_hidden_dim for separate heads. A custom MAAC head requires the original model_config={"critic_value_head_hidden_dim": ...} in the trainer constructor. Continuing the same value-learning setup also requires the original critic_type ("v" or "q").
Training State# Users can enable training checkpoints through train(checkpoint_dir=...) and resume a compatible trainer with resume_from_checkpoint:
# Save a checkpoint at each completed training boundary. trainer.train(checkpoint_dir="./checkpoints", checkpoint_interval=1) # Recreate the trainer with the same models, tokenizers, data, and callbacks. resumed_trainer.train( resume_from_checkpoint="./checkpoints/checkpoint-1", checkpoint_dir="./checkpoints", checkpoint_interval=1, )Checkpoints preserve model and optimizer states, training progress, and random states, along with preference-learning data and history where applicable.
Checkpoints are saved at completed epochs, iterations, or preference-learning stages, with a final save at completion. checkpoint_interval controls periodic saves. Resuming repeats any work since the last checkpoint.
num_train_epochs and num_iterations count the total run, including completed work, and can be increased when resuming. Models, tokenizers, data, and training settings must remain compatible. Stateful datasets and callbacks can provide state_dict() and load_state_dict(); external service state is not restored.
If a preference-learning output directory already contains files, resumed output goes into a resume-* subdirectory.
For W&B, users can merge the saved run identity into their existing wandb_config before constructing the trainer. This preserves logging and output settings and avoids opening an empty run during construction:
from comlrl.utils import read_checkpoint_metadata checkpoint = "./checkpoints/checkpoint-1" identity = read_checkpoint_metadata(checkpoint)["wandb"] if identity and "id" not in wandb_config and "resume" not in wandb_config: wandb_config = {**wandb_config, **identity, "resume": "allow"} # Pass wandb_config to the trainer constructor before resuming.Explicit id or resume settings take precedence. If the checkpoint contains no W&B identity, the helper returns None for wandb and the existing configuration is kept.
Checkpointing is disabled by default: train() without checkpoint options saves no training checkpoints. save_model() exports models only; it does not save the full state needed to resume training.

title: Multi-Agent Actor-Critic
content:
Actor-Critic (AC) methods are widely used policy gradient methods that use critics to support training. AC methods can achieve lower variance and better sample efficiency than REINFORCE, but this requires careful design and tuning of the critic to ensure stable training. In Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), Actor-Critic methods include Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (MAAC) and Independent Actor-Critic (IAC).
MAAC# Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (MAAC) uses one Centralized Critic (CC) across agents to evaluate joint histories with critic_type="v", or joint history-action pairs with critic_type="q". The critic receives the agents’ prompts joined into a single text sequence; Q mode also includes their generated completions.
The critic prediction is denoted by \( C_{\boldsymbol{\phi}}(x_t) \), where \( x_t=\mathbf{h}_t \) in V mode and \( x_t=(\mathbf{h}_t,\mathbf{a}_t) \) in Q mode. CoMLRL forms a one-step target and a TD residual for each agent:
\[ y_{i,t}=\tilde r_{i,t}+\gamma m_t\bar C(x_{t+1}), \qquad A_{i,t}=y_{i,t}-\bar C(x_t), \] where \( \bar C \) is the detached prediction recorded during rollout collection, and \( m_t \) is 1 only when another turn was collected. The final collected turn, including an early-terminated or single-turn rollout, uses \( y_{i,t}=\tilde r_{i,t} \) without bootstrapping. Rewards may be shared across agents or supplied per agent. Here \( \tilde r_{i,t} \) denotes the processed reward, with the optional reference-KL penalty subtracted when enabled.
The actor and critic minimize the following losses over each agent’s mini-batch \( B_i \):
\[ \mathcal L_{\pi_i}=-\frac{1}{|B_i|}\sum_{t\in B_i}\log\pi_{\theta_i}(a_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})\,\operatorname{sg}(\widehat A_{i,t}), \qquad \mathcal L_C=\frac{1}{|B_i|}\sum_{t\in B_i}\big(C_{\boldsymbol{\phi}}(x_t)-y_{i,t}\big)^2. \] Here \( \widehat A \) is the optionally normalized residual and \( \operatorname{sg} \) means stop-gradient. The completion log-probability is the sum of generated-token log-probabilities; prompt and trailing padding tokens are excluded. The loss then averages across samples. Buffers are grouped by agent and turn before updating, and advantage_normalization normalizes the residuals within each such group. Targets and advantages remain fixed during the update. The shared critic is updated sequentially with each agent’s batch, and value_loss_coef scales its loss.
The animation below follows one MAAC turn from sampling through the update for two agents. Both actors use residuals from the same centralized critic, which is then trained against the TD targets using each agent’s batch in turn; IAC instead gives each agent its own critic.
MAAC training step Each agent samples one response per turn; the centralized critic turns the reward and next history into TD targets and residuals that weight each actor's loss and regress the critic. Complete diagram Play Replay In Q mode, the implementation uses the same TD-residual actor weight, with a sampled next action in the bootstrap. It does not implement a separate actor objective weighted directly by Q or a state-only baseline for Q.
MAACConfig Parameters num_agents: Number of agents num_turns: Number of turns critic_type: Critic target type (v for V(h), q for Q(h,a)) num_train_epochs: Number of training epochs agent_learning_rate: Learning rate for agents critic_learning_rate: Learning rate for the shared critic value_loss_coef: Weight on critic loss advantage_normalization: Whether to normalize advantages before updates rollout_buffer_size: Number of samples to collect per agent before an update train_batch_size: Mini-batch size within each update max_new_tokens: Maximum tokens to generate per completion temperature: Temperature for sampling top_p: Top-p for nucleus sampling top_k: Top-k for sampling num_generations: Number of generations per prompt per agent external_prompt_passthrough: Whether to use external prompts directly in multi-turn training discount: Discount factor for the next-turn critic prediction in TD targets; logged expected_return uses undiscounted reward sums early_termination_threshold: A rollout ends after a turn whose mean processed reward exceeds this threshold; None disables early stopping eval_interval: Evaluation interval (in training batches) eval_num_samples: Number of evaluation samples per interval eval_batch_size: Evaluation DataLoader batch size logging_steps: Minimum number of joint-action reward evaluations between training metric logs parallel_training: none for one device or mp for explicit agent/critic device placement agent_devices, critic_devices: Device assignments, required in mp mode reference_kl_enabled, reference_kl_coef: Whether the frozen-reference KL reward penalty is enabled, and its weight (disabled by default) reference_devices: Optional device placement for reference models MAACTrainer Parameters agent_model or agents: Actor model identifier string for homogeneous agents, or list of agent models (multi-agent agent_model must be a string) critic_model or critics: Required single shared critic, supplied as an identifier, model instance, or 1-element list tokenizer: Shared tokenizer, or a per-agent list when using agents; required with agents or a model instance, otherwise loaded from agent_model reward_func: Callable returning rewards (required) reward_processor: Optional reward post-processor formatters: Single callable or list for per-agent prompt formatting args: Instance of MAACConfig (optional) train_dataset: Training dataset (required) eval_dataset: Optional evaluation dataset model_config: Model loading options; critic_value_head_hidden_dim configures the centralized critic’s value head (optional) wandb_config: Weights & Biases logging configuration (optional) metrics_callback: Optional callback taking rollout samples and returning a dictionary of scalar metrics external_transition: Transition function required when num_turns > 1 MAAC updates on collected samples without importance sampling or policy-ratio clipping. MAACConfig has no value_clip_range option. The shared critic uses the first agent’s tokenizer, which must be compatible with the critic model.
The trainer uses a fixed training DataLoader batch size of 1. For num_turns > 1, an external_transition and num_generations=1 are required. train_batch_size defaults to rollout_buffer_size; actual updates use the available samples in each agent/turn group, including smaller groups when buffers are flushed.
IAC# Independent Actor-Critic (IAC) optimizes each agent’s policy with its own critic; other agents serve as part of the environment. Rewards can be shared or agent-specific. The critic conditions on that agent’s prompt/history in V mode, or on its prompt and completion in Q mode. IAC uses the same detached-target convention as MAAC:
\[ y_{i,t}=\tilde r_{i,t}+\gamma m_t\bar C_i(x_{i,t+1}), \qquad A_{i,t}=y_{i,t}-\bar C_i(x_{i,t}), \] where \( x_{i,t}=h_{i,t} \) in V mode and \( x_{i,t}=(h_{i,t},a_{i,t}) \) in Q mode. The actor uses the same sample-averaged loss and completion-token sum as MAAC, with optional normalization within each agent/turn group. The Q-mode actor also uses this TD residual.
CoMLRL supports two IAC variants:
Separate Critic: Uses an independent model for value estimation. Actor and critic parameters are optimized separately, at the cost of storing an additional model per agent.
Shared Model: Attaches a small value head to the transformer backbone, sharing the actor model’s history (or history-action) representations to reduce space requirements.
The critics are updated by minimizing the TD error:
\[ \mathcal L_{C_i}=\frac{1}{|B_i|}\sum_{t\in B_i}\big(C_{\phi_i}(x_{i,t})-y_{i,t}\big)^2. \] When using a shared model (use_separate_critic=False), the actor and value head optimize the combined loss \( \mathcal L_{\pi_i}+\texttt{value\_loss\_coef}\,\mathcal L_{C_i} \). Unless value_clip_range=None, the value loss takes the larger error from the current prediction and a prediction clipped relative to the rollout value, for either critic type:
\[ \ell_{C_i}=\max\Big((C_{\phi_i}(x_{i,t})-y_{i,t})^2,\ (C_{\phi_i}^{\mathrm{clip}}(x_{i,t})-y_{i,t})^2\Big), \\ C_{\phi_i}^{\mathrm{clip}}(x)=\bar C_i(x)+\operatorname{clip}\big(C_{\phi_i}(x)-\bar C_i(x),-\epsilon,\epsilon\big), \] where \( \epsilon \) is value_clip_range and these errors are averaged across the mini-batch. Separate critics use the unclipped squared error.
IACConfig Parameters num_agents: Number of agents num_turns: Number of turns num_train_epochs: Number of training epochs agent_learning_rate: Learning rate for agents critic_learning_rate: Learning rate for separate critics; shared models use agent_learning_rate for both actor and value head value_loss_coef: Coefficient for value loss value_clip_range: Value clipping range in shared-model mode; None disables clipping advantage_normalization: Whether to normalize advantages rollout_buffer_size: Number of samples to collect before an update train_batch_size: Mini-batch size for policy updates max_new_tokens: Maximum new tokens to generate temperature: Temperature for sampling top_p: Top-p for nucleus sampling top_k: Top-k for sampling num_generations: Number of generations per prompt per agent use_separate_critic: Whether to use a separate critic model critic_type: Critic target type (v for V(h), q for Q(h,a)) critic_value_head_hidden_dim: Hidden dimension for critic value head value_head_hidden_dim: Hidden dimension for value head in shared-model mode external_prompt_passthrough: Whether to use external prompts directly in multi-turn training discount: Discount factor in TD targets; logged expected_return uses undiscounted reward sums early_termination_threshold: A rollout ends when a turn’s mean processed reward exceeds this threshold; None disables early stopping eval_interval: Evaluation interval (in training batches) eval_num_samples: Number of evaluation samples per interval eval_batch_size: Evaluation DataLoader batch size logging_steps: Minimum number of joint-action reward evaluations between training metric logs parallel_training: none for one device or mp for explicit agent/critic device placement agent_devices, critic_devices: Device assignments; mp requires agent_devices and, for separate critics, critic_devices reference_kl_enabled, reference_kl_coef: Whether the frozen-reference KL reward penalty is enabled, and its weight (disabled by default) reference_devices: Optional device placement for reference models IACTrainer Parameters agent_model or agents: Model identifier string for homogeneous agents, or list of agent models (multi-agent agent_model must be a string) critic_model or critics: Critic identifier, model instance, or list of critic models when use_separate_critic=True tokenizer: Shared tokenizer, or a per-agent list when using agents; required with agents or a model instance, otherwise loaded from agent_model reward_func: Callable that returns a list of floats (required) reward_processor: Optional processor to apply to rewards formatters: Single callable or list of per-agent callables for formatting dataset items into prompts args: Instance of IACConfig (optional) train_dataset: Training dataset (required) eval_dataset: Evaluation dataset (optional) model_config: Model configuration dictionary (optional) wandb_config: Configuration for Weights & Biases logging (optional) metrics_callback: Optional callback taking rollout samples and returning a dictionary of scalar metrics external_transition: Optional transition function required for multi-turn training IAC updates on collected samples without importance sampling or policy-ratio clipping. In shared-model mode (use_separate_critic=False), value heads are attached to the actor models; passing critic_model or critics raises an error, and value_clip_range only applies in this mode. Agents may be homogeneous or heterogeneous. In separate-critic mode (use_separate_critic=True), users can supply a critics list of length num_agents or a single critic_model source for broadcasting. Distinct model instances or an identifier loaded separately for each critic keep their parameters independent; broadcasting one preloaded model object reuses its parameters. Each critic consumes its actor’s token IDs, so a different critic model must be compatible with that actor’s tokenizer.
The trainer uses a fixed training DataLoader batch size of 1. For num_turns > 1, an external_transition and num_generations=1 are required. train_batch_size defaults to rollout_buffer_size; actual updates use the available samples in each agent/turn group, including smaller groups when buffers are flushed.

title: Multi-Agent RLHF
content:
Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (MARLHF) fits a joint reward model to preference pairs, then trains the policies with RL using the learned reward. CoMLRL generates the preference labels with the task reward_func.
The training flow is: task items → preference pairs → Stage 1: joint reward learning → Stage 2: policy reinforcement learning. Because the reward model scores the team’s complete response, separate actors learn from one shared reward. MADPO instead optimizes the policies directly from the pairs, without a reward model.
In the diagram, both agents’ responses are scored together and ranked into pairs; Stage 1 fits the reward model on these pairs, and Stage 2 trains each policy on advantages from the frozen model.
MARLHF training flow Preference pairs fit a joint reward model, whose frozen scores then train both policies with RL. 1 · Reward learning 2 · Policy learning Pairs Reward model New samples Shared reward RL update Agents Frozen Complete diagram Play Replay Preference Pairs# Each agent \( i\in\mathcal{I}=\{1,\ldots,n\} \) samples \( a_{i,t}\sim\pi_{\theta_i}(\cdot\mid h_{i,t}) \) from its local history; the responses form the joint action \( \mathbf{a}_t=\{a_{1,t},\ldots,a_{n,t}\} \) with joint history \( \mathbf{h}_t \). Only a single turn is currently supported (horizon \( H=1 \)), so \( h_{i,0} \) is agent \( i \)’s prompt and \( \mathbf{a}_0 \) is the joint response.
For each task item in train_dataset, every agent samples preference_num_candidates responses from its formatted prompt. Responses with the same candidate index form a joint response and share one reward from reward_func (after the optional reward_processor). For two joint responses with different rewards, the response with the higher reward is the winner \( w \) and the other the loser \( l \); ties are discarded. Each pair \( (\mathbf{h}_H^{w},\mathbf{h}_H^{l}) \) contains the two joint histories for one task.
The base trainer collects the pairs once, before either stage; preference_pairs_per_sample and pair_selection determine which non-tied pairs are retained for each task. If no task yields a non-tied pair, training returns without fitting a reward model or updating the policies.
MARLHF currently requires num_turns=1 and joint_mode="aligned", even when the selected RL backend supports multi-turn training.
Stage 1: Joint Reward Learning# The JointRewardModel \( \widetilde{R}_{\psi}(\mathbf{h}_t,\mathbf{a}_t) \) concatenates all agents’ prompts and responses into a single text input and applies a scalar head to the causal-LM backbone’s last hidden state at the final non-padding token. Reward learning minimizes the Bradley–Terry loss over the training pairs \( \mathcal{B} \):
\[ \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{RM}}(\psi) =-\mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{h}_H^{w},\mathbf{h}_H^{l})\sim\mathcal{B}} \left[\log\sigma\left(\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\Big[\widetilde{R}_{\psi}(\mathbf{h}_t^{w},\mathbf{a}_t^{w})-\widetilde{R}_{\psi}(\mathbf{h}_t^{l},\mathbf{a}_t^{l})\Big]\right)\right], \] where \( \sigma \) is the sigmoid function. The loss raises the winner’s score relative to the loser’s; it does not regress onto the task reward values.
By default, both the backbone and the head are trained; reward_freeze_backbone=True trains only the head.
Stage 2: Policy Reinforcement Learning# After Stage 1, \( \widetilde{R}_{\psi} \) is fixed. The policies generate \( G \) new joint responses per task (num_generations), \( \widetilde{R}_{\psi} \) scores them without gradients, and the selected backend updates the policies with these shared rewards. With the default rl_algorithm="magrpo", the advantage of response \( g \) is its reward minus the group mean:
\[ \widetilde{A}^{(g)}=\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\left[\widetilde{R}_{\psi}(\mathbf{h}_t^{(g)},\mathbf{a}_t^{(g)})-\frac{1}{G}\sum_{g'=1}^{G}\widetilde{R}_{\psi}(\mathbf{h}_t^{(g')},\mathbf{a}_t^{(g')})\right]. \] Each agent \( i \) weights its own log-probabilities \( \log\pi_{\theta_i}(a_{i,t}^{(g)}\mid h_{i,t}^{(g)}) \) by \( \widetilde{A}^{(g)} \), which the default advantage_normalization=True also divides by the group’s standard deviation. Equation 5 of the MAPL paper scales \( \widetilde{A}^{(g)} \) by \( G/(G-1) \), which equals the "marloo" advantage.
rl_algorithm selects the backend:
Algorithm Policy-training backend "magrpo" MAGRPO with mean-centered advantages; the default "mareinforce" REINFORCE with raw returns "maremax" MAGRPO-family updates with the maximum-reward baseline "marloo" MAGRPO-family updates with a leave-one-out baseline "maac" Multi-Agent Actor-Critic with a joint critic "iac" Independent Actor-Critic with per-actor critics or attached value heads The Multi-Agent REINFORCE and Actor-Critic guides describe these updates; every backend uses \( \widetilde{R}_{\psi} \) in place of the task reward during training. This stage is controlled by num_train_epochs and num_generations, separately from reward_num_train_epochs and preference_num_candidates.
Optional frozen-reference KL regularization (reference_kl_enabled, reference_kl_coef, reference_devices) applies only to this stage. For the MAGRPO family, each agent’s sampled KL estimate, scaled by reference_kl_coef, is subtracted from its returns before the baseline and normalization.
Evaluation# For every backend, evaluation scores responses with the task reward_func (and reward_processor), not with \( \widetilde{R}_{\psi} \), so it reports task scores rather than predicted rewards.
Configuration# Users can import MARLHFConfig and MARLHFTrainer from comlrl.trainers.preference.
MARLHFConfig Parameters num_agents: Number of agents in decentralized mode, or task roles in centralized mode collaboration_mode: "decentralized" (default) or "centralized" preference_num_candidates: Candidates sampled per task and actor for preference collection; at least 2 preference_pairs_per_sample: Maximum pairs retained per task, or None for no limit pair_selection: "reward_gap" selects pairs with the largest reward gaps, "random" selects a random subset, and "all" retains every non-tied pair; "all" requires preference_pairs_per_sample=None max_new_tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k: Candidate generation settings reward_model_name: Model identifier for the reward backbone; defaults to the actor model identifier when available reward_model_device: Reward-model device; defaults to "cuda:0", or None to use the trainer device reward_learning_rate, reward_num_train_epochs, reward_train_batch_size: Reward-model optimization settings reward_max_length: Optional token limit for the combined reward-model input reward_freeze_backbone: Trains only the scalar reward head when True rl_algorithm: Online policy-training algorithm; defaults to "magrpo" num_generations: Online samples per prompt and actor (the group size); at least 2 for the MAGRPO family, or at least 1 for MAAC/IAC num_train_epochs, agent_learning_rate: Online policy-training epochs and learning rate rollout_buffer_size, train_batch_size: Online rollout buffer and update batch sizes; train_batch_size defaults to rollout_buffer_size parallel_training, agent_devices: Policy execution mode and device placement critic_model_name, critic_learning_rate, critic_devices: Critic settings for an actor-critic backend critic_type: "v" or "q" for an actor-critic backend use_separate_critic: Choice of separate critics or actor-attached value heads for IAC value_loss_coef, value_clip_range: Critic loss weight and IAC shared-value-head clipping, as described in Actor-Critic reference_kl_enabled, reference_kl_coef, reference_devices: Optional frozen-reference regularization for the online RL stage eval_interval, eval_num_samples, eval_batch_size: Evaluation schedule and sample sizes for the selected backend logging_steps: Training logging interval MARLHFConfig inherits the shared preference settings from MADPOConfig; MARLHF does not use dpo_beta.
MARLHFTrainer Parameters agent_model or agents: Model identifier for homogeneous agents, or a list of model identifiers or instances num_agents: Number of agents or task roles; must match args.num_agents tokenizer: One tokenizer, or one per actor train_dataset: Task items for preference collection and online policy training eval_dataset: Optional evaluation dataset reward_func: Required callable returning one shared task reward per aligned joint response reward_processor: Optional post-processing of task rewards during preference collection and evaluation formatters: One prompt formatter shared by all roles, or a list of role-specific formatters args: MARLHFConfig instance model_config: Optional model loading configuration wandb_config: Optional Weights & Biases configuration eval_logger, eval_aggregator: Optional evaluation metrics hooks, as in MAGRPOTrainer centralized_comparator_adapter: Prompt builder and response parser for centralized actors or comparators critic_model or critics: Optional critic sources for the MAAC/IAC backend. critic_model must be a model identifier string. Users can supply loaded model instances through critics, using a one-element list for MAAC or one entry per actor for separate-critic IAC. Without explicit sources, critic_model_name or the actor model identifier is used metrics_callback: Optional custom metrics callback for the actor-critic backend reward_model_name is required when the actors are model objects without a model identifier. MAAC and separate-critic IAC likewise require explicit critic sources or a usable critic model identifier.
Collaboration and Iterative Training# Decentralized MARLHF trains separate actors against one joint reward model. With collaboration_mode="centralized", one actor generates the complete joint response. num_agents must equal the number of task roles, and the configuration requires one actor and tokenizer. \( \widetilde{R}_{\psi} \) scores the joint text, which is parsed into role responses only for task rewards and evaluation. Training Framework describes the layouts and adapter interface.
MARLHFIterTrainer repeats preference collection, reward learning, and policy RL. Each iteration \( \nu \) with training pairs fits a newly initialized reward model on the selected pairs \( \mathcal{B}^{(\nu)} \) and then runs Stage 2. New comparisons are labeled with the task reward by default; preference_scoring_reward="reward_model" uses the most recently fitted reward model instead, falling back to the task reward until one exists. An iteration is a refresh-and-training round, not a dialog turn.
Training Framework describes the iterative configuration, the comparator, and the replay buffer that selects \( \mathcal{B}^{(\nu)} \).
